national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet today gave its approval to the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme- NSAP for five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with a total outlay of 53,428 crore rupees. The approval also includes renaming of this scheme and sub-schemes with revision in eligibility criteria, coverage and rate of assistance for divyangjan pension and continuation of pension schemes for old aged and widows and family benefit scheme in its existing form. The National Social Assistance Programme has been renamed as Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana. The Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme will now be named as Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana, while the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme will become Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana.The Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme has been renamed as Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana and while the National Family Benefit Scheme will be called Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana. Briefing media after the Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishanw said that the amount of assistance under divyangjan pension scheme will now be 375 rupees for the age group of up to 79 yrs and 625 rupees for 80 yrs and above. Mr Vaishanw said that the criteria for benchmark disability will be 40 percent against 80 percent at present for divyangjan. He said, under it , the minimum age criterion for the disability pension will now be since birth. He informed that a total of three crore and 20 lakh beneficiaries across all the 36 States and UTs will be benefitted from this approval. He said, Pension schemes for old aged and widows and family benefit scheme will continue in its existing form. The guidelines consisting of the change in eligibility criteria, number of beneficiaries and rate of assistance under divyangjan pension will be issued and implemented within three months.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 102 India expresses solidarity with Saudi Arabia by condemning attacks on civil infrastructure
national_raw_news.content: India today expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and condemned the string of attacks in the West Asian nation. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal condemned the attack on the Aramco headquarters which took place yesterday, saying India condemns all such attacks on civil infrastructure in the country. He said, such attacks are totally unacceptable and must cease immediately. Mr Jaiswal further stated that India stands in solidarity with the people and government of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty. He said, India hopes that peace and normalcy return in the region. Giving an update on the diaspora in Saudi Arabia, Mr Jaiswal said Indian Embassy in Riyadh is in regular touch with Indian community members for their welfare. At the same time, advisories have been issued. He said there have been disruptions in the flight schedule after the attack on the Riyadh international airport. The spokesperson said Indian carriers have been impacted but flight operations of several Saudi airlines are continuing between India and Saudi Arabia. Replying to a query on India-Iran NSA talks, the spokesperson said NSA Ajit Doval spoke to his Iranian counterpart, Dr Mohsen Rezaei on 12th of October. He said they discussed bilateral issues, the regional situation and international developments. He said the safety and security of Indian seafarers and Indian tankers were also raised during the conversation. On OHCHR’s recent remarks on the situation in the national capital, Mr Jaiswal said the concerns are unwarranted and unacceptable. He called out OHCHR for their selective approach as they have not reacted in their public positions on protests which are happening or law enforcement actions which are happening in other parts of the world. He cautioned that if they continue on this path, it will lead to loss of faith in multilateralism. He added that it also undermines their credibility as an organisation.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Regional News 167 Maharashtra govt announces Rs 5000 to each farmer in drought-affected talukas
national_raw_news.content: Maharashtra has declared 305 of its 358 talukas drought-hit, following the addition of 40 more talukas to the list. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has announced that farmers will receive initial financial assistance of five thousand rupees in their bank accounts before Diwali. Speaking to reporters after the state cabinet meeting in Mumbai today, Mr Fadnavis said all 12 standard drought relief concessions would be extended to the 305 affected talukas. These include crop loan restructuring, land revenue concessions, subsidies on electricity bills and fee exemptions for farmers’ children. The Chief Minister said cooperative banks and credit societies had been warned against coercive loan recovery or harassment of farmers. Similar efforts were being made to ensure that private banks and financial institutions followed the same approach. He added that groundwater levels in Marathwada had fallen below three metres, necessitating early deployment of water tankers, which would be tracked through GPS. The state has also disconnected nearly 16 thousand illegal water connections to protect drinking water supplies. On fodder availability, Mr Fadnavis said reserves ranged from 90 days to seven months, depending on the region. The government has assured farmers that fodder harvested in suitable areas would be purchased at the Minimum Support Price. Meanwhile, Higher and Technical Education Minister Chandrakant Patil has directed colleges across the state not to charge examination fees to students from drought-affected talukas. Any fees already collected must be refunded, failing which strict action will be taken against the institutions. The directions were issued during an online meeting with vice-chancellors of state public universities in Mumbai today to review examination-related issues and other academic matters.

national_raw_news.title: IEA says repeated attacks in Gulf make oil supply recovery fragile 3 hours ago 54
national_raw_news.content: Global oil supply is projected to decline by 5.8 million barrels per day (bpd) to an average of 100.7 million bpd this year, before rebounding by 7.7 million bpd in 2027. However, the International Energy Agency (IEA) has warned that renewed attacks in the Gulf have made the recovery fragile. According to the IEA’s monthly Oil Market Report released today, global oil supply increased by 2.5 million bpd month-on-month in September, driven by Gulf producers. However, the IEA noted that the recent escalation in attacks on regional energy infrastructure and tanker traffic threatens to derail further gains. Meanwhile, the IEA forecast that oil demand would fall by an average of 2.6 million barrels per day in 2026. Diesel is expected to account for 25 per cent of that demand drop amid restricted product availability, soaring fuel prices and a deteriorating economic outlook linked to the West Asia conflict. Although global diesel prices have eased from the all-time highs of more than 200 dollars per barrel reached last month, yet benchmarks remain nearly double the price of crude oil and their pre-crisis levels. The agency noted that diesel markets remained under significant strain as prolonged supply disruptions forced counter-seasonal stock draws ahead of autumn refinery maintenance and peak winter demand. Global oil demand is projected to recover by 2 million barrels a day next year, less than its previous forecast of 2.6 million bpd.

national_raw_news.title: J&K: Navratri Utsav adds vibrant blend of devotion and culture to festive atmosphere in Katra 2 hours ago 37
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, more than 1.80 lakh devotees have visited the Shri Mata Vaishno Devi shrine in the Trikuta Hills in Katra since the beginning of Navratri. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that during the first three days alone, 1,41,888 pilgrims paid obeisance at the holy shrine and sought the blessings of Mata Vaishno Devi. The pilgrimage has continued amid the devotional atmosphere of Navratri. Arrangements are in place to facilitate pilgrims visiting the shrine during the festival period. Devotees are undertaking the journey to the holy cave shrine, while Katra-the base camp for the pilgrimage, is also hosting a series of cultural and devotional programmes. The Navratri Utsav 2026 is being celebrated in Katra after a gap of two years. The return of the festival has added to the festive atmosphere in the town, bringing together pilgrims and visitors for a programme of religious, cultural and community events. A key attraction is Mata Di Kahani, which offers visitors a devotional programme centred on the story and significance of Mata Vaishno Devi. The festival also features an All-India Devotional Songs Competition, providing a platform for devotional performances and music. Together, these events complement the spiritual journey made by pilgrims during Navratri. Visitors can also explore a multimedia exhibition depicting various sponsored schemes. The exhibition uses visual and multimedia displays to present information about the schemes to attendees. A Shobha Yatra is another highlight of the celebrations, bringing colour and pageantry to the festival programme in Katra. With the continuing flow of pilgrims and the return of the Navratri Utsav, Katra is witnessing a vibrant blend of devotion and cultural celebration.

national_raw_news.title: UP govt to give sugar at concessional rate of Rs 52/kg 2 hours ago 53
national_raw_news.content: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to provide sugar to the public at a concessional rate of rupees 52 per kg. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath held a meeting with officials of the Sugar Industry and Department of Sugarcane and Cane Development to review sugar prices and issued special instructions to ensure that the public does not face any inconvenience. Following the Chief Minister’s directions, the Sugar Industry and the Department of Sugarcane and Cane Development will provide sugar to the public at a concessional rate of just 52 rupees per kg. Consumers can avail themselves of this facility at the sugar sales centre of the Sugar Corporation/Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation located on the premises of the Lal Bahadur Shastri Ganna Kisan Sansthan. The prices of 1 kg and 2 kg packets are rupees 52 and rupees 102, respectively. The prices of 5 kg and 50 kg packets have been fixed at rupees 250 and rupees 2,500, respectively. According to the department, this special sugar sale will operate regularly on every working day. Citizens can avail the facility by visiting the sugar sales centre on the Ganna Kisan Sansthan Parisar between 10 am and 5 pm. All necessary arrangements have been completed at the sales centre to ensure convenience and smooth purchases for consumers. Consumers can purchase sugar according to their daily requirements. The Department of Sugar Cane and Cane Development appealed to the residents of the state capital to make maximum use of this public welfare initiative. Under the guidance of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the department remains committed to providing similar practical relief to the public in the future

national_raw_news.title: Punjab police arrest main accused in Parvinder Singh Jhota’s murder 3 hours ago 322
national_raw_news.content: A day after anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota was shot dead in Punjab’s Mansa district, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann announced that the main accused, Chemist Ashwani Kumar has been arrested and assured that none involved in this broad daylight murder of the anti-drug activist will be spared. He said he has directed the Director General of Police to take strict and appropriate action against those involved. Police arrested the accused, from Rajasthan late last night. Mansa district administration demolished his house today. The irate mob, including those sitting on dharma in protest against the killing since yesterday, vandalized his medicine shop. A large number of police personnel have been deployed to maintain law and order. Various political parties including Shiromani Akali Dal and Congress have condemned the killing and the deteriorating law and order situation in the state. BJP State President, Kewal Singh Dhillon, during a press conference, today, blamed the Aam Aadmi Party government in the state for prevailing law less ness. He said Chief Minister Mann is himself holding the portfolio of the home department. The killings of innocent people including police personnel are being reported almost every day and gangsters are freely moving and drugs are selling everywhere.
